article.title: Number of Students From Crisis-Stricken Countries Rising
article.summary:
Despite significant declines in overall international student applications and enrollment since the start of the second Trump administration, the number of students in the United States from crisis-stricken countries has increased since 2024, according to a new analysis of international student data.
The growth is likely driven by refugee and displaced students from Nepal, Colombia and Iran, all countries that have recently been devastated by natural disasters or political upheaval.
The report doesn’t include students with temporary protected status; those designated as refugees, asylum seekers or humanitarian parolees; or other displaced students already living in the U.S.
Despite the jump in students from Columbia and Nepal, the countries from which the Trump administration has restricted travel sent far fewer students in 2026.
Laura Wagner, director of refugee student initiatives at the Presidents’ Alliance, said the data reveals how policies such as travel bans affect refugee students.

article.title: Cox’s Bazar: Rohingya Life in Exile
article.summary:
Inside the world’s largest refugee camp, Rohingya families fight hunger and loss as aid dries up, clinging to faith, each other and the hope of returning home.
For more than a million Rohingya refugees, Cox’s Bazar was meant to be a place of safety.
Together, they face shrinking food aid, restricted opportunities, separation from loved ones and no clear route home.
The Islamic holy month of Ramadan forms the backdrop, bringing moments of faith, family and communal ritual into sharper relief amid mounting hardship.
Made with a Rohingya producer and director of photography living in the settlement, the film offers an intimate view from within: people working, studying, creating and caring for their families while fighting to preserve their dignity.

article.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with Online Table Repacking and Query Planning Controls
article.summary:
The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19, introducing changes to database maintenance, query planning, replication, and application development.
PostgreSQL 19 also introduces pg_plan_advice and pg_stash_advice , extensions that let administrators influence query plan selection and apply stored advice to queries by identifier, without changing application code.
Logical replication now supports sequence values, and PostgreSQL automatically raises the effective WAL level to logical when the first logical replication slot is created.
PostgreSQL 19 also warns after successful MD5 password authentication.
PostgreSQL 19 is available now.
